title: Three Homilies on the Dormition of the Mother of God
author: John of Damascus
blurb: Three sermons John of Damascus preached at Mary's tomb in Gethsemane on her falling asleep. The second quotes the Euthymian History, which tells how the apostles opened her tomb after the third day and found it empty. A fresh English translation of all three homilies.
first_english_note: Earlier English translations exist (among them Brian Daley's, 1998, in copyright, not used); this is a fresh English translation from the Greek of PG 96.

text_history.method: English translated from the Greek of Migne, Patrologia Graeca 96, cols. 699-762, transcribed from the page images of the archive.org scan; the scan's OCR is too garbled to use. Where the printed Greek is plainly wrong, the English follows the reading that the sense and Migne's facing Latin require; each such place is listed below. Psalm numbers are given in the English (Hebrew) numbering.

joins.note: Printed διαιρέσεως ('division'); the English follows προαιρέσεως ('a good will'), with the facing Latin 'probaque voluntate'.

Printed ἐνδέδυμαι ('I have put on') is read as ἐκδέδυμαι ('I have put off' the garments of skin), with the facing Latin 'exui'; printed ὑπερέρχεται is read as ὑπέρχεται ('undergoes'); printed ἀχειροτμήτῳ is taken in the sense 'not made by hands'.
Printed θέσματα ('ordinances') is rendered 'wills', with the facing Latin 'voluntates'.
Printed 'our hands' is read as 'my hands', since Mary is speaking (facing Latin 'manuum mearum').
Printed ἀμελητί ('carelessly') is read as ἀμελλητί ('at once').
Printed ἐλαίου ('oil') is read as ἐλέου ('mercy'), as Migne's own note directs; printed γεύμασιν is read as ῥεύμασιν ('in their flowing'), with the facing Latin 'fluentis'.
Printed κλίματι is read as κλίμακι ('ladder'), ἐδείξατο as ἐδέξατο ('received'), and 'fruits of the presence' as 'the bread of the presence', each with the facing Latin.
